proposals.title: No query_execution knob change is justified: GetUserTweets terminal saturation is structural (fully cached, index-driven read path), not a planner/executor misconfiguration
proposals.configuration_cause: None attributable to any allowed query_execution knob. The incumbent plan evidence is an Index Scan with estimated_rows=1.0 and estimated_total_cost=8.45, i.e. the planner already picks the only sensible access path; the read side is fully cache-resident (buffer_hit_ratio 0.9999265, blks_read 20.1/s, blks_hit 273328/s) with seq_scan=0.0/s, temp_files=0.0/s, temp_bytes=0.0, deadlocks=0.0/s and lock_waiting_backends 0 at every percentile, so there is no observable mis-estimation, spill, or lock stall for default_statistics_target / random_page_cost / seq_page_cost / work_mem / jit / parallelism to correct.
proposals.mechanism: Closed-loop terminal-budget identity: goodput_rps ~= terminals / weighted-mean client latency = 8 / 283us ~= 28.3k rps, which reproduces the measured 28257 rps. GetUserTweets is ~90% of the transaction mix (3048834 of ~3.4M transactions) at a 169us p50 / 278us mean on a fully cached index path (9.67 buffer hits/txn, 7.27 tuples fetched/txn, blk_read_time 7.2e-6 ms/txn, zero temp bytes), so it owns 0.884 of the finite 8-terminal budget. That cost is per-query executor CPU on hot shared buffers plus the client round trip; the statement never enqueues on the WAL commit path (wal_write_per_txn 0.0075, wal_bytes_per_txn 5.17B) and never waits on a lock. Consequently no knob in the query_execution set changes the dominant term: the tail (p99 2813us) has no accompanying I/O, lock, or WAL signal to attribute it to.
proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets performs an index access returning ~7 rows per transaction entirely from shared buffers; no sequential scans, no sorts or temp spills, no heap-read stalls and no lock acquisition beyond instantaneous buffer pins. Its latency is fixed per-query planner+executor CPU plus client round trip, which none of the allowed planner/statistics/executor knobs reduce without an observable defect to correct.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: unchanged within +/-5% of the incumbent band 29762.6-31906.7 rps (median 30213.6); the 28257 rps observation is a low draw of the same configuration, not a configuration regression.
proposals.expected_latency_effect: unchanged; GetUserTweets p50 ~169us and overall p95 ~754us stay within the observed replicate spread (baseline p50 157-169us, p95 646-696us).

predictions.rationale: Closed-loop identity 8 terminals / 283us mean = 28.3k rps matches the measured 28257 rps. With knob_changes=[] the configuration is bit-identical to the incumbent, so throughput must stay within +/-5% of the 29762.6-31906.7 rps replicate band; the current 28257 rps is inside the run-to-run spread already seen across baseline_1..3 (7% band).

0.8838 = 848.4s of 960s of terminal time at ~3.05M transactions; baselines were 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787. With identical config, count (~3.05M) and mean latency (278us) are unchanged, so the fraction stays ~0.88 within +/-5%; no query_execution knob alters transaction frequency or the cached-read mean.

p50 169us is a shared-buffer index access (0.9999265 hit ratio, 9.67 blks_hit/txn, 7.2e-6 ms blk_read_time/txn, 0 temp bytes). No allowed knob changes the executor path for this Index Scan (est_rows 1.0, est_cost 8.45); baseline p50s were 165/169/157us (+/-4%), so a 10% tolerance is conservative.

Measured WAL write average 0.138ms with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, wal_sync=0.0/s and wal_sync_time_per_txn=0.0; the wal_wait alert rests on one instantaneous sample (wal_waiting_backends median 0, p95 0, max 1 of ~9 backends) and on 5.17 WAL bytes/txn. anomaly.aggregation: max over the measured window (median 0.0, p95 0.0)

proposals.configuration_cause: None of the incumbent's memory/storage knobs is causal for the flagged anomaly. (1) wal_sync_method=open_datasync makes every WAL write a device-synchronous O_DSYNC write, so the flush cost is folded into wal write latency and sync_average_ms is null by construction; the alert's slow-fsync branch therefore cannot be read directly off the counter set and must be judged from wal_timing.write_average_ms, wait events and host_io together. (2) commit_delay=671 with commit_siblings=12 is inert: with 8 terminals, numbackends max 9, active_backends median 6/p95 9 and idle_in_transaction max 5, the sibling gate is never reached, so no transaction is delayed and the pair cannot explain any tail. (3) checkpoint_timeout=100 with checkpoint_completion_target=0.833 and max_wal_size=3672 MB yielded only ~1 timed checkpoint per 161 s run, with checkpoint_write_time=checkpoint_sync_time=0 and buffers_checkpoint=6.56/s. (4) bgwriter_delay=22, bgwriter_lru_maxpages=338, bgwriter_flush_after=143, checkpoint_flush_after=177 and backend_flush_after=83 are bounded-writeback settings, yet buffers_clean=0/s with dirty_bytes median 3.45 MB and writeback_bytes p95 45 kB: there is nothing to write back. (5) shared_buffers=53504 pages (418 MB) is sufficient: buffer_hit_ratio 0.99993, blks_read 20.1/s, blk_read_time 0.20 ms/s. (6) work_mem=15776 kB and temp_buffers=10139 are never exercised: temp_files=0 and temp_bytes=0.
proposals.mechanism: Disk-side demand per client transaction is about one microsecond: wal_write_time_per_txn 0.0010384 ms, wal_bytes_per_txn 5.17 B, blk_read_time_per_txn 7.17e-6 ms, checkpoint_write_time_per_txn 0, checkpoint_sync_time_per_txn 0, temp_bytes_per_txn 0. Even at the per-write level the cost is small: 0.1379 ms x 212.7 WAL writes/s = 29.3 ms of device-synchronous write per second (2.9% of one core-second) with PSI io some/full stall fraction 0.0, io_waiting_backends p95 1/max 1 and exactly one instantaneous sample (wal_waiting_backends max 1 of ~9 backends) showing a WAL waiter. The throughput-limiting class GetUserTweets (3,048,834 of ~3.42M transactions, terminal_capacity_fraction 0.8838) is read-only and therefore never enqueues on the WAL flush path at all; its mean (278 us) exceeds its median (169 us) because of a non-storage p99 (2813 us) that no allowed memory/storage knob can address. The smallest coherent knob group for the storage mechanism actually diagnosed here is the empty set: any edit to wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay/flush_after, wal_sync_method, commit_delay/commit_siblings, bgwriter pacing or checkpoint spacing would be an unfalsifiable perturbation of a subsystem currently delivering microseconds of work per transaction.

proposals.query_effect: No plan or access-path change: plan_evidence is an Index Scan (estimated_rows 1, cost 8.45) with 9.67 buffer hits and 7.1e-4 block reads per transaction, and no memory/storage knob in the allowed set alters access-path selection for GetUserTweets or the InsertTweet insert path. Expected query effect: none.
proposals.expected_tps_effect: No change is expected from the memory/storage domain. A re-measurement should land inside the incumbent's own replicate band (28257.5-31906.7 goodput_rps, verified median 30213.6), i.e. within +-10%. The only lever that could move TPS is the non-storage tail of GetUserTweets, which is outside this domain.
proposals.expected_latency_effect: None for GetUserTweets (p50 169 us / p99 2813 us are cache-resident, executor-side micro-stalls on a read-only class), and no measurable effect for InsertTweet, whose p99 of 3999 us is not fsync-bound when the entire WAL write budget is ~1 us per client transaction and the per-write device latency is 0.138 ms.

predictions.rationale: Closed-loop identity 8 terminals / ~283 us weighted mean latency reproduces the observed 28257 rps; with knob_changes=[] the re-measurement must stay inside the incumbent's own replicate band (28257.5-31906.7 rps, verified median 30213.6). A +-10% window brackets the 12.9% max/min spread already observed across the three incumbent replicates.

GetUserTweets consumed 0.8838 of terminal capacity (incumbent replicates 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787; span 0.51 pp) at a 169 us median while its storage cost is 7.2e-6 ms of block read time and 0 temp bytes per transaction; this read-only class never touches the WAL, checkpoint or bgwriter paths, so no allowed memory/storage knob can shift the fraction by 1 pp.

Measured 0.1379 ms mean per WAL write with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, blk_read_time 0.2027 ms/s and checkpoint write/sync time 0. The WAL write path has no queue to relieve (212.7 writes/s, 146.1 kB/s), so the mean per-write latency should not move by 0.5 ms.

The flagged wait is a single instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends over 148 samples. Reconfiguring an unstressed WAL pipeline cannot remove a waiter that is not present beyond the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 backend or more.

InsertTweet p99 is 3999 us on 0.0075 WAL writes and 5.17 WAL bytes per client transaction, with the whole WAL write budget at ~1 us per client transaction and no recorded fsync time (sync_average_ms null because open_datasync folds the flush into write). The commit durability path is not the tail driver, so its p99 should stay within the +-20% span already observed across replicates (3336-3999 us).

alternatives.statement: The 0.1379 ms mean WAL write latency is an under-sampled device flush cost: because wal_sync_method=open_datasync folds the fsync into write() and sync_average_ms is null, the wal_wait alert could be the leading edge of a storage-latency mechanism that grows with writer concurrency.
The 2813 us p99 of GetUserTweets is backend clock-sweep eviction of dirty buffers stalling readers that pin the same pages, i.e. background-writer/checkpoint pacing rather than the WAL path.

The observation run's 28257 rps versus 29762.6-31906.7 rps across the incumbent replicates is client/terminal-side variance (idle_in_transaction p95 3 / max 5, client_waiting_backends p95 4 of 9 backends), not a server memory/storage effect.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: per-class wait_event sampling plus EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for the exact GetUserTweets SQL to attribute the 2813 us p99 to executor/LWLock/client effects before any storage knob is considered.
concurrency_maintenance: confirm that the 0.8838 terminal share is a frequency effect (no lock waits, conflicts 0.0, locks_waiting 0) so that no maintenance knob is proposed against it.
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim to exceed the incumbent; it prevents an evidence-free reconfiguration of an unstressed storage subsystem (wal_buffers, wal_sync_method, commit_delay/commit_siblings, bgwriter/checkpoint spacing) that would consume measurement budget and could perturb the very tail that limits TPS. Its value is diagnostic: it converts the high-severity wal_wait alert into a falsifiable, zero-cost statement (wal_write_time_per_txn ~1 us, write_average_ms 0.138, PSI io stalls 0.0, one waiter sample) so that the remaining budget goes to the path that actually owns 0.8838 of terminal capacity.

locks_waiting median/p95/max = 0/0/0, lock_waiting_backends max 0, deadlocks 0/s and conflicts 0/s; with no knob change and 8 terminals there is no lock conflict to create or relieve, so this stays at 0 backends.

Dead-tuple generation is 0.08/s and autovacuum_count is 0.0248/s against autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.128 on a cache-resident read-mostly snapshot; holding the incumbent autovacuum knobs leaves that background rate within 25% of 0.0248/s over a 120s window.

alternatives.statement: The wal_wait alert is a genuine WAL write/fsync stall that one instantaneous observation under-resolves, so a WAL/commit-path knob (e.g. wal_sync_method, wal_writer_delay/wal_writer_flush_after, commit_delay/commit_siblings) would help.

The GetUserTweets p99 (2813us, vs 169us median) is caused by lock-manager or buffer-LWLock contention among the 8 concurrent terminals on hot index pages, which the terminal_capacity_fraction framing hides.

The replicate-to-replicate throughput spread (28,257.5 vs 31,906.7 rps) is produced by autovacuum/checkpoint background writeback stealing CPU/IO from the read path, which vacuum/checkpoint knobs would fix.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) plus wait_event sampling on the exact GetUserTweets SQL to attribute its 2813us p99 tail (executor vs LWLock vs client idle).
memory_storage: confirm the WAL/commit path needs no change; this proposal refutes a slow-fsync cause via wal_timing, wait events and host_io together.
proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not exceed the incumbent; it refuses an unjustified change and protects a verified-healthy configuration. Acting on the single-sample wal_wait alert would perturb a write path that costs 0.0072 WAL writes and 0.00104 ms of WAL write time per transaction, and acting on vacuum knobs where dead tuples accrue at 0.08/s has no mechanism. The only evidence-supported action is to hold the incumbent and confirm the frozen no-change predictions; an intervention here would add restart/reload risk and measurement cost for a predicted null effect.

The tail is a rare per-call micro-stall (GetUserTweets p99 2813us, but GetTweetsFromFollowing max 32,155us with fraction 0.0386), not a queue: lock_waiting_backends and locks_waiting are identically zero, so no wait queue exists for any lock, connection, vacuum or WAL knob to drain. The 'waiting_backends' gauge (median 2 / p95 7 / max 7) decomposes into client_waiting_backends (max 5, i.e. closed-loop client idle, consistent with idle_in_transaction max 5) plus io_waiting_backends max 1 plus wal_waiting_backends max 1; it is not lock or WAL backpressure.
